questions.question: If a trailer starts to jackknife, what should the driver do?

options.text: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
Should firmly apply the brakes.
Can straighten the trailer with the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes so the trailer wheels can grip the road again. Do not use the trailer hand brake. Applying the brakes caused the wheels to lock up in the first place.

questions.question: What is true about combination vehicles?

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Usually require less skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Usually require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over than single vehicles.

questions.question: Before a trip, how can you check that air reaches all trailers?

options.text: Checking for moving air inside of each trailer.
Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feeling for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. Listen for air escaping. If you hear air, the air brake system is supplying all trailers correctly.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, what may happen?

options.text: May lean during turns.
May add extra support during turns.
May be easier to steer during turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: May lean during turns.
questions.explanation: A load on one side of a trailer causes it to lean that way. This increases the risk of rollover during turns and lane changes.

questions.question: When coupling, after connecting the air lines to the trailer, what should you do next?

options.text: Supply air to the trailer.
Activate the emergency brake.
Disconnect the glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: After connecting the air lines during coupling, you should supply air to the trailer. This is part of the correct coupling procedure.

questions.question: What should you do before beginning a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.
Remove the relay valves.
Close the emergency line valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the emergency line valve.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that air reaches all trailer brakes by opening the rear valves and listening for air. Then close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake and connects to the ____ valves.

options.text: Relay
Supply
Emergency

questions.correctAnswerText: Relay
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which let the trailer brakes work quickly.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, what should you do?

options.text: Make quick, sudden changes.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Accelerate by pushing the accelerator to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves.
questions.explanation: Steer gently and smoothly when driving with a trailer. Avoid sudden movements to reduce the risk of tipping over.

questions.question: When should a trolley valve be used?

options.text: Should be used while driving.
Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
Should be used when parking uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trolley valve works the trailer brakes and should only be used to test them. Do not use it while driving—it can cause a skid. Do not use it while parking—it may release air pressure and let the brakes fail.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, which trailer should be directly behind the cab?

options.text: Lightest
Heaviest
Smallest

questions.correctAnswerText: Heaviest
questions.explanation: Place the heaviest trailer closest to the tractor. Put the lightest trailer at the rear.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside a trailer.
Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
questions.explanation: Heavy cargo that is too high makes a vehicle easier to roll over. Keep cargo weight as low as possible in the trailer to reduce this risk.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than usual.
Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
Push the brake pedal more lightly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: Use the brake pedal the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up.
It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
It makes turning a vehicle easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS stops your wheels from locking up during hard braking. If the system detects wheels about to lock, it reduces brake pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: During a trip, the ____ should be open.

options.text: Rear service line shut-off valve
Rear supply line shut-off valve
Inner shut-off valves

questions.correctAnswerText: Inner shut-off valves
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, all shut-off valves must be open except the last valve on the rear trailer. This allows air to reach all brakes without escaping from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: Combination vehicles are usually:

options.text: Easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Lighter than single commercial vehicles.
More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: If you are backing and the trailer begins to drift off-course, the driver should:

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, fix it right away by turning the top of the steering wheel in the direction the trailer is drifting.

questions.question: When coupling:

options.text: You can assume all vehicles are the same.
Be sure that you are coupling correctly.
Cracks in the mounting are acceptable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure that you are coupling correctly.
questions.explanation: Incorrect coupling and uncoupling can be very dangerous.

questions.question: The best way to recognize that your trailer has started to skid is by:

options.text: Seeing other drivers' faces.
Checking the trailer in your mirrors.
Feeling the trailer move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors to see if your trailer is skidding. This is the easiest way to notice a skid early.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To test the trailer brakes.
To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.
To accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: To test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor without a trailer
A tractor attached to two trailers
A tractor with a tank

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor without a trailer
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer attached. Drivers should be cautious when operating a bobtail tractor.
